question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees get?
expected_answer: 28 days a year, including bank holidays (more with long service, up to 30).
ai_answer: Full-time employees get 28 days of paid annual leave each leave year, including bank holidays. Long-service days are added on top: 1 extra day after 3 years' continuous service (29 days in total) and 2 extra days after 5 years' continuous service (30 days in total), with a maximum entitlement of 30 days. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement based on contracted hours.

question: When do we get paid?
expected_answer: Monthly, on the last working day of the month.
ai_answer: Employees are paid monthly on the last working day of the month, per Employee Handbook §1-6. Payslips are available in StaffHub.

question: How long is the probation period for new starters?
expected_answer: 6 months, with reviews at 3 and 6 months; can be extended by up to 3 months.
ai_answer: New employees have a 6-month probation period, with review meetings with their manager at 3 months and 6 months. Probation may be extended by up to 3 months if more time is needed. During probation the notice period on either side is 1 week.

question: What is the mileage rate if I use my own car for work?
expected_answer: 45p per mile (normal commuting can't be claimed).
ai_answer: Mileage in a personal car is paid at 45p per mile under the Expenses Policy (§1-6). Normal commuting to your usual workplace cannot be claimed. Claims must be made in ExpenseHub within 30 days of the cost being incurred, with an itemised receipt, and claims made more than 90 days late will not be paid.

question: How long does my password need to be?
expected_answer: At least 14 characters, with MFA wherever supported.
ai_answer: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long, according to the Information Security Policy (v2025.1), section 1-5.

question: How quickly must a customer complaint be acknowledged?
expected_answer: Within 2 working days (final response within 8 weeks).
ai_answer: A customer complaint must be acknowledged within 2 working days, according to the Customer Complaints Procedure (v2025.1). The final response must be sent within 8 weeks.

question: How much company sick pay do I get if I've worked here for 4 years?
expected_answer: 4 weeks at full pay in any rolling 12 months (after probation), on top of SSP.
ai_answer: After 4 years' service you get 4 weeks of company sick pay at full pay, in any rolling 12-month period, on top of SSP, once you have completed probation. The passages do not say how this interacts with any other sick pay limits beyond what is stated.

question: What support can I get for studying a qualification?
expected_answer: Course fees up to £1,000 a year and up to 5 days' paid study leave, after probation.
ai_answer: Employees who have passed probation can apply through LearnHub for study support for a qualification relevant to their role. This covers course fees of up to £1,000 per year and up to 5 days of paid study leave per year for exams and study. Applications must be approved by your line manager and the Head of Learning and Development. Travel and accommodation for approved training are claimed under the Expenses Policy, and course fees are paid directly by the company and must not be claimed as expenses. If you leave within 12 months of a course finishing you must repay 100% of the course fees, or 50% if you leave between 12 and 24 months after it finishes.

question: If I leave 18 months after the company paid for my course, do I have to pay anything back?
expected_answer: Yes, 50% of the course fees (leaving between 12 and 24 months after the course).
ai_answer: Yes, you must repay 50% of the course fees. Under the Training and Development Policy, if you leave between 12 and 24 months after the course finishes, you must repay 50% of the course fees (leaving within 12 months requires repaying 100%). This applies to study support; the passages do not say whether the same repayment rule applies to other paid courses, and the 18-month period is measured from when the course finished, not when it was paid for.

question: Is there an allowance for working from home?
expected_answer: £26 a month for employees contracted to work remotely at least 1 day a week.
ai_answer: Yes. Employees whose contract says they work remotely at least 1 day a week receive a home working allowance of £26 a month, paid through payroll. Office-based support roles may work remotely for up to 2 days a week with their line manager's agreement.

question: Can I roll over unused holiday into next year?
expected_answer: Yes, up to 8 days, which must be used by 30 June.
ai_answer: Yes, up to 8 days of unused annual leave can be carried forward into the next leave year without needing approval, and they are shown automatically in StaffHub from 2 January. Carried-forward days must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, otherwise they are lost and not paid. Carrying forward more than 8 days is only allowed in limited cases (long-term sickness, family leave, or business reasons with written approval from the Head of People), with up to 20 days allowed; sickness-related days must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year they were earned, and other exceptional days by 30 June.

question: I clicked a dodgy link in an email. What should I do?
expected_answer: Report it to the IT Service Desk immediately (and use Report Phish for suspicious emails).
ai_answer: Report it as an IT and data incident. A phishing click is listed under IT and data incidents, which must be reported to the IT Service Desk within 1 hour. You can contact the IT Service Desk through StaffHub or on extension 4357.

question: Can I keep the tips a punter gives me at the blackjack table?
expected_answer: No. Gaming staff tips go in the tronc box and are shared through the tronc scheme.
ai_answer: No. Gaming employees must never keep tips personally. All tips given to gaming employees are placed in the tronc box at the table and shared through the tronc scheme. Only hospitality employees follow their venue's tipping process instead.

question: How quickly do I have to report a lost company laptop?
expected_answer: Immediately, and in any case within 1 hour, to the IT Service Desk.
ai_answer: A lost or stolen company device must be reported to the IT Service Desk immediately, and in any case within 1 hour of noticing it. Reporting quickly allows the device to be wiped remotely.

question: What happens to my annual leave if I'm ill while I'm on holiday?
expected_answer: With a fit note, those days count as sickness and the leave is given back. Report it on day one.
ai_answer: If you are ill during booked annual leave and provide a fit note covering the days of sickness, those days are treated as sickness absence and the annual leave is returned to you. You must report the sickness on the first day, following the sickness reporting steps in section 2 of the Sickness Absence Policy (phone your line manager or duty manager, at least 1 hour before your usual start time for office-based staff or at least 2 hours before your shift for gaming floor, security and cage staff). The policies do not say what happens if you are ill during leave but do not provide a fit note.

question: Where do I report a customer I think is laundering money?
expected_answer: Directly to the MLRO with the internal suspicious activity report form, not SafeLog; never tell the customer.
ai_answer: Do not report suspected money laundering in SafeLog, and do not discuss it with the customer or with colleagues who do not need to know. Report it directly to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) using the internal suspicious activity report form, sent on the same day, as described in the Compliance Guidelines. Do not investigate yourself and do not tell the customer, as tipping off is a criminal offence.

question: Can I claim my course fees back on expenses?
expected_answer: No. Course fees are paid directly by the company under the Training Policy.
ai_answer: No. Course fees for approved training are paid directly by the company under the Training and Development Policy and must not be claimed as expenses. The Expenses Policy also lists training course fees among items that cannot be claimed. Travel and accommodation for approved training can be claimed under the Expenses Policy instead.

question: Someone on the gaming floor looks under 18. What do I do?
expected_answer: Ask for photo ID (Think 25), tell the duty manager immediately, and log it before the end of the shift.
ai_answer: Ask the person for valid photo ID (Think 25 applies, since anyone who appears under 25 must show valid photo ID) and tell the duty manager immediately. Nobody under 18 may enter the gaming floor. Log the incident in SafeLog before the end of your shift.

question: I was off sick for months last year and couldn't use my leave. How much can I carry over and by when?
expected_answer: Up to 20 days because of long-term sickness, to be used within 18 months of the end of that leave year.
ai_answer: Under the standard rule you can carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave, and these must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, or they are lost. Because you were on long-term sickness, you may carry forward more than 8 days, up to 20 days in total. Days carried forward because of sickness must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned. The passages do not say whether the extra days need approval, so check with HR.

question: Can gaming floor staff take two weeks off over Christmas?
expected_answer: No. 24 Dec to 1 Jan is a peak period; at most 5 consecutive days, and only with the General Manager's approval.
ai_answer: No, not as one continuous two-week break. During peak periods (24 December to 1 January), gaming floor and security employees may take no more than 5 consecutive days of leave, and only with approval from their venue's General Manager. Leave must also be requested at least twice its length in advance (for example, 5 days needs 10 days' notice), and requests made after a rota is published can only be approved if cover is available. The passages do not say whether separate blocks of leave over the Christmas period are allowed in total.

question: How much notice do I need to give to book a week of annual leave?
expected_answer: Twice the length of the leave, so 10 days for 5 days of leave; later if the rota is already published.
ai_answer: You must give at least twice the length of the leave you are requesting. For a week (7 days) of annual leave, submit your request through StaffHub at least 14 days before the first day of leave. Gaming floor and security requests made after the rota is published (4 weeks in advance) can only be approved if cover is available, and managers should respond within 5 working days.

question: How much annual leave can I carry forward?
expected_answer: Up to 8 days, used by 30 June (the 2024 rule of 5 days by 31 March no longer applies).
ai_answer: Employees can normally carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year, and these must be used by 30 June or they are lost and not paid. No approval is needed for up to 8 days. More than 8 days can be carried forward only if the leave could not be taken due to long-term sickness, maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave, or business reasons where the manager cancelled approved leave and the Head of People approved the exception in writing. In those cases up to 20 days may be carried forward. Days carried forward due to sickness must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned; other exceptional carry-forward must be used by 30 June. question: How many days a week can office staff work from home?
expected_answer: Up to 2 days with manager agreement; Tuesday and Wednesday are office days (not 3, as in 2023).
ai_answer: Employees in office-based support roles (for example Finance, HR, IT, Compliance and Marketing) may work remotely for up to 2 days a week, with their line manager's agreement. Tuesday and Wednesday are anchor days, when office-based employees are expected to be in the office unless on leave or agreed otherwise with their manager.

question: Am I allowed to work from abroad for a few days?

Each trip must be approved in advance by your line manager and the Information Security team, and requested through the IT Service Desk at least 2 weeks before travel. Passage P1 also requires a company laptop and the company VPN, and confidential work must not be done where screens can be overlooked. The passages do not say whether gaming floor, cage, security, hospitality or customer service roles can work abroad at all.
